mission: 建立 Doré 全站共享 translation faculty：核心只保留 provider-neutral TranslationRequest/Segment/Context/Result；黎明書局、多寫及未來版塊各自擁有符合自身產品行為的翻譯浮現界面。優先本地、離線、無按量 API 成本、可替換 provider。
constraints: provider licenses must be tracked separately from runtime code licenses
Bible Scripture text remains excluded from Dawn Library translation product

explored.fit: very strong for low-latency client-side translation where a required language pair/model exists
explored.limits: language/model coverage is narrower than a single 400+ language multilingual model; model packages must be managed on demand

facts: supports Marian, OPUS-MT, M2M-100, NLLB, mBART, MADLAD-400 and other encoder-decoder families
explored.fit: strongest common runtime candidate; lets Doré change models without changing the translation faculty contract
explored.limits: runtime is not itself a translation model

facts: CTranslate2 conversions already exist in community
explored.fit: high for broad foreign-language -> Chinese coverage and avoids NLLB's non-commercial model license
explored.limits: heavier than pair-specific Marian/Bergamot; benchmark on actual historical theological prose before defaulting

explored.fit: strong for common high-volume pairs such as English/European languages -> Chinese when a good pair model is available
excellent bootstrap/fallback and useful architecture to absorb for model package management
explored.limits: pivoting can degrade literary/theological translation quality; should not become the sole quality path

explored.fit: useful API behavior/reference, not necessary to embed as Doré core
explored.limits: embedding the whole service adds a duplicate server/product layer and AGPL considerations

facts: model card says research-oriented and not released for production deployment
explored.fit: valuable benchmark/reference for low-resource language quality
explored.limits: non-commercial restriction conflicts with keeping the core broadly reusable; do not make it the default dependency

architectureDecision.principle: absorb mature runtimes, not whole products
architectureDecision.core: Doré Translation Faculty + existing Context/Lexicon/Retrieval/Capability Router
architectureDecision.routing: select provider by source language, installed model, rights/license, device capability, latency, quality profile and section surface; keep provider invisible to product UI

qualityStrategy.historicalBooks: Translate semantic segments, not isolated sentences. Doré Context supplies author/work/period/neighbor segments/terminology/proper names.
qualityStrategy.traditionalChinese: Provider output passes through zh-Hant normalization and Doré terminology memory; do not create a fake Chinese Edition.
qualityStrategy.progressive: render source immediately; translate viewport and adjacent segments; cache eligible results by workId+witnessId+segmentId+provider/model/version+context-profile.
qualityStrategy.benchmark: Build a small gold set from actual Dawn holdings: patristic English, Latin, Greek, Syriac-via-English, Reformation/early-modern English, modern English. Compare faithfulness, names/terms, syntax, zh-Hant readability, latency and memory.

loadReduction: Only Translation Faculty contract and model registry are resident. Models are lazy-loaded/on-demand and can be evicted. Browser Bergamot models are downloaded/cached only when needed; server/local CTranslate2 loads only selected model. This follows the project rule: capability grows while resident burden shrinks.

surfaceProjection.dawn-library: book-reading translation: original / zh-Hant / bilingual stable-segment comparison
surfaceProjection.dore-folio: writing-side selected text/document translation using the same core faculty but its own UI and editing semantics
surfaceProjection.future: other sections may expose translation only when their product structure calls for it; no universal floating translator UI

nextImplementation: Add provider-neutral translation model registry and CTranslate2/Bergamot adapter contracts under dore_core; do not download model weights yet. Then benchmark MADLAD-400 vs OPUS-MT/Argos on a real Dawn Library sample before choosing default routes.
